# Volume 3 — Chapter XX Hugh Speaks

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“This has been a dull, prosy day,” Cressy yawned, lazily stretching out upon the sofa after first ousting a pair of highly offended cats.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0000 }

Nell raised her eyes from Pickwick Papers. Having completed her spring examinations, she was indulging in Dickens as a treat.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0001 }

“This day was mundane for our part,” she uttered reflectively, “yet for others it was extraordinary. Someone experienced blissful joy during it. Maybe a monumental act occurred somewhere today—or an incredible poem was composed—or an important man was brought into the world. And a heart was crushed, Cressy.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0002 }

“Honey, why did you ruin your nice idea by adding that final sentence?” complained Cressy. “Broken hearts—or any disagreeable topic—are things I prefer not to think about.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0003 }

“Do you believe you will manage to avoid disagreeable matters your whole life, Cressy?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0004 }

“Good heavens, no. Aren't I facing them at this moment? Surely you wouldn't consider Hector and Orlando agreeable, would you, when they do nothing but make my life a misery?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0005 }

“Cressy, you do not ever treat anything with seriousness.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0006 }

“Why ought I to? A sufficient number of people do so. Individuals such as myself are required by the world, Nell, merely to entertain it. Were every person to be intellectual, grave, and profoundly, solemnly serious, it would be an awful place. The purpose I have is, in the words of Josiah Allen, ‘to charm and allure.’ Admit it now. In this previous winter, has not existence at Tabby’s Place actually been far brighter and more agreeable owing to my presence here to lighten all of you?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0007 }

“Indeed, it has,” admitted Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0008 }

“And every one of you loves me—including Aunt Euphemia, who considers me completely insane. For what reason, then, ought I to attempt to change? Oh, goodness, I am terribly drowsy. My eyes were open until one o’clock last night because I was engrossed in a chilling tale about a phantom. I perused it while lying in bed, and once I completed it do you imagine I was able to step out of bed so I could extinguish the light? I was not! Had Mabel not luckily arrived late that lamp would have continued to burn well and brightly right up to the morning. The moment I caught the sound of Mabel I summoned her inside, clarified my dilemma, and persuaded her to extinguish the lamp. Had I stepped out to accomplish it on my own I was certain that something would clutch my feet as I climbed back inside. On another note, Nell, has Aunt Euphemia made up her mind regarding her plans for this summer?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0009 }

“Yes, she will remain here. I am aware that she is doing this for those dear cats, despite her claim that unsealing her home is an excessive burden, and her aversion to staying as a guest.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0010 }

“What is it that you’re reading?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0011 }

“Pickwick.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0012 }

“A book like that perpetually stimulates my appetite,” Cressy remarked. “It contains such a abundance of delicious food. It appears the characters are constantly feasting upon ham and eggs alongside milk punch. Reading Pickwick usually prompts me to forage through the cupboard. Just thinking about it makes me realize I am famished. Do we have any delicacy in the pantry, Queen Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0013 }

“This morning I baked a pie made of lemon. A slice of it can be yours.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0014 }

Cressy rushed away toward the pantry and Nell, alongside Smudge, went off to the orchard. It was a damp, delightfully fragrant night in the beginning of spring. The snow in the park had not completely disappeared; a small, dirty mound of it still remained beneath the pine trees along the harbor road, protected from the warmth of April suns. This sustained the mud on the harbor road and cooled the night air. Nevertheless, green grass was sprouting in protected areas and Hugh had discovered some faint, fragrant arbutus within a concealed location. Carrying a handful of it, he walked up from the park.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0015 }

Perched upon the large gray rock in the fruit garden, Nell gazed at the poetic sight of a leafless birch branch suspended with complete elegance before the light red dusk. In her imagination, she was constructing a grand structure—a marvelous residence with sun-drenched courtyards and grand chambers filled with the fragrance of Araby, where she held power as ruler and mistress. Seeing Hugh approach across the fruit garden made her scowl. Recently, she had succeeded in avoiding being alone in Hugh's presence. However, he had cornered her completely this time; and even Smudge had abandoned her.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0016 }

Taking a seat next to her on the rock, Hugh offered his Mayflowers to her.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0017 }

“Nell, do these not bring back memories of home and the picnics from our former school days?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0018 }

Nell accepted them and pressed her face into their depths.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0019 }

“At this exact instant, I am located within Mr. Silas Mott’s barrens,” she declared with pure delight.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0020 }

“I take it you will actually arrive there in several days?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0021 }

“No, not for two weeks. I am intending to stay with Cressy in Harborough prior to returning home. You will reach Brierley ahead of me.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0022 }

“No, Nell, I will not spend any time in Brierley during this summer. Since I have received an offer for a position at the Daily News office, I intend to accept it.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0023 }

“Oh,” Nell replied absentmindedly. She pondered how an entire summer at Brierley would feel in Hugh’s absence. For some reason the thought displeased her. “Well,” she finished in a dull tone, “it is certainly beneficial for you.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0024 }

“Indeed, I had been wishing to obtain it, as it will prove beneficial to me in the coming year.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0025 }

“You ought not to overwork yourself,” uttered Nell, absent-mindedly stating whatever came to mind. Her heart longed for Cressy to emerge. “Your studies have been so continuous during this past winter. Is this night not lovely? Imagine this: beneath that gnarled, ancient tree over there, I chanced upon a bunch of white violets today. It gave me the sensation of unearthing a mine of gold.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0026 }

“It is a habit of yours to continually find gold mines,” Hugh remarked—likewise inattentively.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0027 }

“We should walk over and check whether we are able to discover any others,” Nell enthusiastically proposed. “Cressy will be summoned by me and—”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0028 }

“Do not concern yourself with Cressy and the violets at this moment, Nell,” Hugh said gently, holding her hand so firmly that she was unable to pull it away. “I have something to tell you.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0029 }

“Oh, refrain from saying it,” Nell exclaimed in a pleading manner. “Refrain—please, Hugh.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0030 }

“I have to. We cannot continue in this manner anymore. Nell, my love belongs to you. You are aware of that. I—I am unable to express the extent of it. Can you give me your word that you will marry me one day?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0031 }

“I—I am unable to,” Nell uttered sorrowfully. “Oh, Hugh—you—you have ruined it all.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0032 }

“Are you completely devoid of feelings for me?” was Hugh’s inquiry following a most terrible silence, throughout which Nell had lacked the courage to raise her eyes.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0033 }

“No—not like that. You mean a lot to me as a friend, certainly. However, Hugh, I am not in love with you.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0034 }

“Is there no chance, however, that you might offer me a bit of hope for the future?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0035 }

“No, I can’t,” Nell cried out in desperation. “I never, never can love you—in that way—Hugh. This is something you must never mention to me again.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0036 }

Another interval occurred—of such great length and terror that Nell was finally forced to raise her eyes. Hugh’s features were drained of colour right to his lips. And his gaze—Nell trembled, however, and turned her sight elsewhere. This contained no romance. Did marriage offers have to be either absurd or—terrible? Would she be able to erase the memory of Hugh’s countenance?
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0037 }

“Is there anyone besides us?” he inquired finally with a quiet tone.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0038 }

“No—no,” Nell answered with fervor. “I have no affection for anyone of that sort—and my fondness for you surpasses anyone else in the world, Hugh. And it is essential—it is essential that we remain friends, Hugh.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0039 }

A small, harsh laugh escaped Hugh.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0040 }

“Comrades! Nell, I am unable to be fulfilled by your friendship. It is your love that I desire—yet you inform me that it will always be out of my reach.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0041 }

“Forgive me, Hugh; I’m sorry,” represented the entirety of what Nell was able to utter. Oh, where, indeed, had gone every one of those elegant and courteous addresses with which she had routinely, in her mind, turned away unwanted suitors?
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0042 }

Hugh softly let go of her hand.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0043 }

“Forgiveness is not required here. I believed at certain moments that you held genuine affection for me. It was merely my own self-deception. Farewell, Nell.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0044 }

Nell made her way to her room, took a seat on her window seat behind the pines, and wept bitterly. A feeling came over her that an incalculably precious element had departed from her life. Naturally, it was Hugh’s friendship. Oh, for what reason did she have to lose it in this manner?
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0045 }

“Honey, what is wrong?” Cressy inquired, stepping inside via the moon-drenched darkness.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0046 }

Nell offered no reply. Just then, she longed for Cressy to be a thousand miles distant.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0047 }

“You have probably gone and turned down Hugh Carrow. Nell Harcourt, you are a fool!”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0048 }

“Is it idiotic to decline marrying someone who holds no place in my heart?” Nell asked with a chilling tone, driven to answer.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0049 }

“You fail to recognize love when it appears before you. Using your imagination, you have fabricated an idea that you believe to be love, and you anticipate that genuine love will resemble it. Look at that, I have just uttered the initial logical remark of my entire existence. I am curious about how I accomplished it?”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0050 }

“Cressy,” begged Nell, “do go away and leave me by myself for a short time. My world has collapsed into ruins. I wish to rebuild it.”
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0051 }

“Lacking any Hugh inside?” asked Cressy, departing.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0052 }

"A world without Hugh!" Nell uttered the phrase mournfully. Might it not turn out to be an extremely desolate, deserted realm? Be that as it may, Hugh was entirely to blame. He had ruined their wonderful friendship. She would simply have to adjust to existing in its absence.
{: #nw-v03-c20-p0053 }
